title: Pinterest Uses Event Time Watermarks to Finalize Petabyte Scale Data Partitions
gist: Pinterest built an event-time partition finalization mechanism in its Flink-to-Iceberg CDC ingestion that publishes a monotonic watermark as an Iceberg table property, letting downstream jobs know when streaming data is complete enough to read. The platform handles petabyte-scale data across thousands of pipelines.

insights.claim: In streaming CDC ingestion there is no job-completion point to signal partition readiness, and data can arrive after a partition's wall-clock interval ended, so Pinterest needed a completeness signal.
insights.speaker: Leela Kumili
insights.so_what: Moving from batch to streaming loses implicit completion guarantees that downstream pipelines relied on.
insights.quote: Unlike the previous batch-based approach, where job completion indicated that a partition was ready

insights.claim: Pinterest's ingestion stack uses CDC, Kafka, Flink, Spark and Iceberg from MySQL, TiDB and KVStore, supporting petabyte-scale data and thousands of pipelines, with online changes available typically in 15 minutes to an hour.
insights.speaker: Leela Kumili
insights.so_what: Gives scale and freshness context for the design tradeoffs.
insights.quote: supports petabyte-scale data and thousands of pipelines

insights.claim: Inside the Flink-to-Iceberg sink, event time is extracted per CDC record and min, max and percentile statistics are collected at checkpoints and stored in the Iceberg snapshot summary, with a t-digest representing the distribution in a few hundred bytes.
insights.speaker: Leela Kumili
insights.so_what: Reusing snapshot metadata makes completeness tracking cheap.
insights.quote: a t-digest representing the distribution in a few hundred bytes

insights.claim: The default policy takes the minimum event time across a configurable number of recent commits and rounds it down to the hour, and percentile-based policies can trade completeness for freshness.
insights.speaker: Leela Kumili
insights.so_what: Teams can tune freshness versus completeness per use case.
insights.quote: Percentile-based policies can trade some completeness for fresher data.

insights.claim: The watermark is monotonic, so late-arriving records cannot move an already published value backward.
insights.speaker: Leela Kumili
insights.so_what: Non-regressing guarantees let downstream consumers safely trigger on it.
insights.quote: The watermark is monotonic, preventing late-arriving records from moving an already published value backward.

insights.claim: Storing the watermark as an Iceberg table property lets downstream sensors read it without a separate coordination service, and Spark propagates it to the base table during CDC upsert commits.
insights.speaker: Leela Kumili
insights.so_what: Co-locating the completeness signal with data removes extra infrastructure.
insights.quote: allowing downstream sensors to read it without a separate coordination service

insights.claim: Finalization is no longer a byproduct of a job finishing but an explicit signal derived from event-time progress.
insights.speaker: Leela Kumili
insights.so_what: Reframes data readiness as a first-class concept in lakehouse streaming.
insights.quote: Finalization is no longer a byproduct of a job finishing.

insights.claim: The design composes existing Flink watermarks and Iceberg snapshots, implemented via accumulators and commit processors in the sink's extensibility points, and an Iceberg issue discusses extending IcebergSink for custom committable metadata.
insights.speaker: Leela Kumili
insights.so_what: Upstream support for sink metadata could standardize this pattern.

insights.claim: An architect at Google calls the non-regressing safe-to-read watermark the elegant part of the design.
insights.speaker: Nitesh Singhal
insights.so_what: Peer validation of the monotonic watermark design.
insights.quote: The non-regressing safe-to-read watermark is the elegant bit here.

insights.claim: The core challenge is getting streaming freshness without losing the guarantees that batch provided.
insights.speaker: Tharun Kumar Reddy Polu
insights.so_what: Batch-to-streaming migrations hinge on rebuilding readiness semantics.
insights.quote: Getting freshness without losing the guarantees batch gave us is the core challenge.
